Subject: Self-signup: Dedicated capacity for Cloudforge

Hi Ben,

I just completed a self-signup trial on Redwood and wanted to follow up directly. We're Cloudforge (ML infra for realtime personalization). We're evaluating Dedicated capacity because our production workload is sensitive to tail latency and we expect sustained high QPS (30-60 qps with 1k token median).

Attached is a short usage snapshot from our pilot (usage_snapshot.csv) to give context. We're hoping to see a live walkthrough focused on:
- dedicated capacity sizing recommendations
- latency profiles at 95/99 pctiles
- fallback routing behavior and autoscale/burst options

Available times this week: Thu (6/10) 11:30–1:00 PDT or Mon (6/14) morning. We're in PST.

Also, procurement will want a one-page MAP and any high-level SLA bullets to share with legal.

Thanks — happy to coordinate a time.

—Alex

Ben — quick answers inline below.

> can you confirm the SLA target you care most about (p50 vs p95 vs p99)
We care about p95 for interactive endpoints (goal < 200ms p95) and p99 is important for a small subset of low-latency endpoints (goal < 500ms p99).

> whether the 1k token median is across the full request or per-step?
That’s per response; many responses are ~1k tokens because we attach context.

> bursty traffic?
We do see bursts, especially at campaign launches — short spikes up to ~150 qps (rarely 200+).

Thursday 6/10 at 12:00 PDT works for us (I'll be on). Maya (procurement) will join to collect the MAP/SLA bullets. Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize by end of Q3.

Thanks — Alex
